findings.title: feature request: a state change reason for clawbacks, which are stored as BURN like a payment to the issuer
findings.short: A clawback is stored as a burn.
findings.cause: The state change vocabulary has no CLAWBACK reason. Clawback and ClawbackClaimableBalance write a BALANCE BURN row (and a DEBIT), so the CAP-67 `clawback` event of the ledger is stored as a `burn`. wallet-backend documents this as intended (docs/architecture/state-changes.md L92), so the draft is a feature request.

findings.title: transaction participants from meta are never collected (participantsForMeta reads the TransactionMeta V0 arm)
findings.short: Accounts that only the transaction meta shows are never recorded as participants.
findings.cause: participantsForMeta switches on `meta.Operations`, the V0 arm of the TransactionMeta union, which is nil for v1 to v4 meta, so accounts that only the meta shows (the sponsor of a claimed or clawed-back claimable balance) are never participants, while accounts only the envelope names (claimants, a payment destination that is the issuer) are. The extra envelope-named participants match wallet-backend's documented rule (docs/architecture/state-changes.md L119-L124); the dropped meta-only ones are the bug. Already reported upstream as #677 (open); the draft is a comment for it with a concrete dropped sponsor.

findings.title: question: BALANCE rows for claimable balance and liquidity pool transfers do not record the balance or pool
findings.short: A transfer to or from a claimable balance or liquidity pool loses its counterparty.
findings.cause: BALANCE rows are written per account; the claimable balance (B) or liquidity pool (L) end of a transfer has no row, so the stored transfer has a null counterparty and the ledger's transfer event to or from the B or L address has no counterpart. The single row is documented (docs/architecture/state-changes.md L67-L68, from #442), so the draft asks whether the B or L address belongs in it.

findings.title: core (xdrpp) accepts a bool word other than 0 or 1 as true and hashes its own re-encoding with 1
findings.short: A bool word other than 0 or 1 is read as true.
findings.cause: xdrpp's xdr_traits<bool>::from_uint is u != 0, and the enum check runs on the converted value, so core decodes any non-zero bool word as true. The transaction hash, the signature check and the protocol 28 rust parse check all use core's re-encoding (word 1), never the submitted bytes. In a local core 30.0.0 run an envelope with the word 2 signed over the canonical hash was applied with txSUCCESS and stored with 1; signed over the submitted bytes it got txBAD_AUTH. Low severity: no authorization bypass or fund loss, but the hash of the submitted bytes differs from core's transaction hash and stellar-xdr reads the same argument as false. The evidence is the three-way split of the SDK answers on the envelope form: some read the word 2 as true like core, stellar-xdr reads it as false, and the rest refuse it (the fuzz classes in findings/fuzz/known-classes.txt are the same root cause).
